summary: (F2) One confirmed sign-in from Turkcell (TR) falls outside the account baseline and is flagged as valid-account use (T1078.004). (F3) Ten likely sign-ins originate from Portugal via university VPN vpn-edge-02 on device LT-3104. The TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token, not user activity. Risk Gate escalates at confidence 0.65 despite no confirmed abuse chain.

actions.action: Force password reset and revoke all sessions for prof.kaya@aegean.edu; require MFA re-enrollment.
Audit LT-3104 and vpn-edge-02 authentication logs to confirm device ownership and check for concurrent logins.
Monitor for additional sign-ins from ASNs outside baseline, especially non-interactive mail-sync tokens.

limitations: Mail-sync token context limits confidence that the TR event represents human compromise; LT-3104 device ownership is unverified.
F3 has no associated ATT&CK technique, restricting tactical enrichment for the Portugal VPN cluster.

risk.rationale: The only confirmed signal (F2: one Turkcell/TR sign-in, T1078.004) is explained as a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not an interactive human logon, so it is not an account takeover chain. The PT sign-ins (F3) align with baseline via university VPN vpn-edge-02 from known device LT-3104. The impossible-travel, password-spray, and VPN KEV exposure claims are all rejected by critics (shared egress with MFA across many accounts; patched firmware; vpn-edge-01 not used by this account). No data-quality conflicts. Suspicious signals are explained away, with no confirmed takeover and no unresolved exposure.
